per_query.query: Seeing a spike in failed lookups from our DNS resolvers, roughly 12% above normal, with clients getting error responses instead of answers. Started around 07:00 UTC and lasted about four hours, concentrated in a few large data centers. Anyone else seeing this?
per_query.likely_cause: Expired DNSSEC signatures in the root zone. The root zone version from 21 September had signatures expire at 07:00 UTC on 4 October 2023. No newer root zone version was available to the resolver systems, so resolvers that could not validate DNSSEC began returning SERVFAIL responses. This matches the 12% rise in SERVFAIL rate, the 07:00 UTC start, and the concentration in large data centers. The excerpts describe a similar public incident (1.1.1.1, October 4, 2023) and do not cover your specific environment, so confirm that your resolvers' root trust anchor and root zone data are the cause before acting.
per_query.suggested_fix: Check whether your resolvers hold a root zone with expired DNSSEC signatures and whether a newer root zone is available to them. Obtain and load a current root zone version so signatures validate again. Then monitor SERVFAIL rates to confirm recovery. Going forward, alert on root zone signature expiry and on failed or stale root zone updates so resolvers do not run on an expired zone. The excerpts do not give a full remediation procedure, so verify the exact steps against your resolver software's documentation.
